_why: Known ideas with relations a textbook would draw, lessons whose new idea should link to a known one, and controls that should link to nothing. Written before the prompts were run against it.

known.name: consistent hashing
known.summary: servers and keys on a ring of hash values, each key going to the next server clockwise

known.name: hash ring
known.summary: the circle of hash values consistent hashing places servers and keys on

known.name: debouncing
known.summary: waiting until the typing stops before running the search, using the search box example

known.name: throttling
known.summary: running a handler at most once per interval, like a turnstile letting one person through a second

known.name: event loop
known.summary: javascript runs one task at a time and picks the next from the queue when the stack is empty

known.name: promises
known.summary: an object standing for a value that arrives later, like an order ticket at a cafe

known.name: binary search
known.summary: halving a sorted range each step until the target is found

known.name: sorted arrays
known.summary: arrays kept in order so that searching can skip most of them

known.name: b tree
known.summary: a wide shallow tree that keeps keys sorted on disk pages

known.name: database indexes
known.summary: a separate sorted structure that lets the database find rows without reading the table

known.name: optimistic locking
known.summary: edit freely and check a version number on save, retrying if someone else saved first

known.name: pessimistic locking
known.summary: take a lock before editing so nobody else can change the row meanwhile

known.name: bloom filters
known.summary: a bit array that says definitely not present or maybe present

known.name: tcp handshake
known.summary: syn, syn ack, ack: three messages before a connection carries data

lessons.question: why does each server get lots of spots on the ring
lessons.title: Virtual Nodes
lessons.explanation: with one spot each, an unlucky server owns a huge arc of the ring. virtual nodes give every server many spots on the hash ring, so the keys spread evenly, and when a server leaves its keys scatter across all the others instead of landing on one neighbour.

lessons.question: what does await actually do
lessons.title: Async Await
lessons.explanation: await pauses this function until the promise settles, then carries on with its value. it is the same promise underneath, written as if it were step by step code, like pausing a recipe while the oven heats.

lessons.question: how does a binary search tree find things
lessons.title: Binary Search Trees
lessons.explanation: every node has smaller keys on its left and larger on its right, so finding a key is a guessing game: go left or right at each node, discarding half of what is left, the same halving as binary search.

lessons.question: how does postgres decide whether to use my index
lessons.title: The Query Planner
lessons.explanation: the query planner estimates the cost of each way to run the query, reading the whole table or walking an index, using statistics about how many rows match, and picks the cheapest route, like a sat nav.

lessons.question: so the rxjs debounceTime operator, is that the same thing
lessons.title: debounceTime in RxJS
lessons.explanation: yes, debounceTime is debouncing: it waits until the stream has been quiet for the given time, then lets the latest value through, which is why your search only fires once they stop typing.

lessons.question: why is my css rule being ignored
lessons.title: CSS Specificity
lessons.explanation: the browser picks the rule with the most specific selector: an id beats a class, a class beats a tag. your class rule loses to the id rule on the same element.
